confirmed: The document title and all listed authors match. The PDF is arXiv:2407.14333v7, stamped 7 January 2026, with manuscript date 8 January 2026; it has 84 pages and includes Appendices A-I on pp. 27-84 (PDF p. 1; p. 27, Appendix A; pp. 66-84, Appendix I). The entire markdown, including appendices, was read.

Both studies are online randomized experiments with individual, between-person assignment to DALL-E 2, DALL-E 3 (Verbatim), or DALL-E 3 (Revised). Model and target task were assigned simultaneously by complete randomization across 45 task-model cells per experiment (PDF pp. 8-9, sections 3-3.1; p. 34, Appendix B.1).

The logo experiment supplies the qualifying randomized creative task: participants created original logos for assigned briefs and their generated output was scored for fulfillment of the brief. Thus has_randomized_people_study=true and context_class=none are appropriate; the paper belongs in the two-screener pipeline (PDF pp. 9, 11-12, sections 3.1 and 3.3-3.3.1; pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2).
Image replication analyzed 1,893 people: DALL-E 2 = 655, DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) = 629, DALL-E 3 (Revised) = 609 (PDF p. 35, Table A.1 sample-size note; p. 46, Appendix C.4).

Logo generation analyzed 1,857 people: DALL-E 2 = 628, DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) = 617, DALL-E 3 (Revised) = 612. Both experiments exceed the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 36, Table A.2 sample-size note; p. 47, Appendix C.5).

The initial raw datasets contain 2,059 people for image replication and 2,067 for logo generation; these are distinct from the final analyzed samples. No separately enumerated total at the moment of assignment or complete initial arm counts were located, supporting the conservative null n_randomized fields (PDF pp. 45-47, Appendices C.4-C.5).

The final samples contain 18,560 image-replication prompts and 18,425 logo-generation prompts, not those numbers of people. The samples follow participant exclusions and prompt filtering; these totals cover all arms and should not be treated as the exact observation counts of each two-arm regression or the enlarged replay/rating datasets (PDF p. 10, section 3.1 and footnote 6; pp. 45-47, Appendices C.4-C.5).

Both samples were fluent English-speaking US Prolific participants. Each experiment allowed up to 25 minutes for at least 10 prompts; participants received one of 15 target images or one of 15 logo briefs (PDF pp. 9-11, sections 3.1-3.3; p. 40, Appendix B.4.3; pp. 41, 43, Appendices B.5.1-B.5.3).

The model descriptions are accurate: DALL-E 3 (Revised) used default hidden GPT-4 prompt rewriting, while Verbatim attempted to suppress rewriting with incomplete compliance. Models were memoryless and participants retained their assigned model (PDF p. 9, section 3.1; p. 38, Appendix B.2).

S1-O1 reported numbers match exactly: DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) versus DALL-E 2 increased CLIP cosine similarity by 0.0164, 95% CI [0.0104, 0.0224], p < 10^(-5), approximately 0.19 standard deviations (PDF p. 14, section 4.1.1 and Figure 1B). This is fidelity to a fixed reference, not an across-person diversity outcome (PDF p. 10, section 3.2.1).

The image-replication analysis uses an expected score per prompt averaged over 10 generated images; original-model and counterfactual replay images support the main-text analyses. Overall ATEs use iteration and target-image fixed effects with participant-clustered standard errors (PDF pp. 10-11, section 3.2.1; p. 45, Appendix C.3; p. 55, Appendix F.1.1).

S2-O1 reported numbers match exactly: DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) versus DALL-E 2 increased Bradley-Terry beta by 0.8075, 95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], p < 10^(-10), approximately 0.57 standard deviations. The regression uses iteration and logo-task fixed effects with participant-clustered standard errors (PDF p. 18, section 4.2.1 and Figure 3B; p. 58, Appendix F.2.1).

Logo quality is an automated output score: gpt-4.1-nano compares fulfillment of the design brief, and Bradley-Terry estimation assigns strength to each generated logo. Pairwise judgments are inputs to the scoring model, not the participant count or the regression observation unit (PDF pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2; p. 59, Appendix F.2.3).

The approximate standardized magnitudes come from z-scored output analyses. Appendix E.2 specifies normalization across both model arms within task-attempt cells, with task-only normalization for across-attempt analyses; Appendix H reports the standardized ATEs (PDF pp. 53-54, Appendix E.2; p. 64, Appendices H.2.1 and H.3.1).

The one-line finding is supported: the logo ATE is 0.8075 with 95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], and the replay-based model effect accounts for approximately 92.7% of the total gain (PDF pp. 18-19, sections 4.2.1-4.2.2). Replay analyses reuse participant prompts and are not additional randomized participant samples (PDF p. 13, section 3.4; p. 45, Appendix C.3).

Prompt similarity measures compare successive prompts or prompts around their own participant-specific centroid, while distributional compression refers to quality scores; neither establishes homogenization of different participants' creative outputs (PDF pp. 50-51, Appendix D.4; pp. 19-20, section 4.2.3). The paper is not a synthesis, so synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF p. 8, section 3).

The original SHORT brief explicitly requires core=unclear for routing to two-screener review and leaves unrequested fields at defaults; these defaults are not independently extracted negative findings (codex-jobs/lscreen-c383/brief.md, lines 20-26). For subsequent full screening, both experiments explicitly state preregistration (PDF p. 41, Appendix B.4.4; p. 43, Appendix B.5.4), and the paper discloses Microsoft research funding and Microsoft/OpenAI author affiliations (PDF p. 1, Author declarations).
summary: The short form's design, participant counts, source version, and reported results match the PDF. The randomized logo-generation experiment analyzed 1,857 people and scored their output quality, warranting two-screener review.
